post.caption: The Taj Mahal's flowers are gemstones. Emperor Shah Jahan built it in Agra for his wife, and work began in 1632, with the main building done by 1648. Its white marble walls are inlaid with colored stones in a craft called pietra dura in Italian, or parchin kari in India. A master drew each pattern on the marble in henna, and craftsmen carved a recess and set in thin slivers of polished stone. Stones include blue lapis lazuli and orange carnelian, and black onyx forms the Quran lettering, each letter carved to fit. Workshops in Agra still make parchin kari.
